source_locator: R2296: B.I.15/a, Zieleniewski, headquarters at Uśnik as of the campaign opening
current_activity: division headquarters at the village of Uśnik
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-01, cited below. Zieleniewski (PISM B.I.15/a, R2296), in both typed copies of his account, says that on the night of 29-30 August 1939 the division moved into the area south of Nowogród and west of Ostrołęka as the reserve of Narew Operational Group, and that division headquarters was at the village of Uśnik. The 1-4 September entry says the division remained that reserve, hidden in the forests, with villages used only as auxiliary billets, until the night of 4-5 September, when it moved to the area southeast of Ostrołęka (no headquarters village is named for that later move). The 1 September pin is Uśnik, still the named headquarters village at the campaign opening. The village lies south of Nowogród; it is east, not west, of Ostrołęka. The sector wording is recorded here without changing the named village. A parent under Narew Operational Group is left blank, because the date that group command ended is not entered on this branch. Event definition: A dated headquarters, movement, engagement or surrender location in the September 1939 campaign. Event support: PISM B.I.15/a (R2296), the typed after-action account of Pułkownik Tadeusz Zieleniewski. Memory account, uneven; used at confidence 0.5. source_locator: R2296: B.I.15/a, Zieleniewski, 17 September, forests west of Włodawa
current_activity: 33rd Reserve Infantry Division reaches the forests west of Włodawa and attacks toward the Bug
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-17, cited below. Zieleniewski (PISM B.I.15/a, R2296) says that on the morning of 17 September 1939 the division reached the forests west of Włodawa, secured a line between the woods and the town, and attacked in an attempt to throw German forces back across the Bug. He later marched on toward the forests by the Sobibór railway station; that overnight stop is entered as C13757. That night he also learned that Soviet forces had crossed the frontier. The Włodawa fighting itself is still against German units, so the operation is Fall Weiss.
